lessons.title: Your First Rack
lessons.concept: Build: a rack needs power and cooling to run. Power is counted in kW, and PUE shows how much extra the hall burns.
lessons.goal: Power a rack, cool it, and run it for three hours.
lessons.passed: A powered, cooled rack ran a job

steps.text: Place a rack on the glowing spot
say: Hi. I'm Bea. I do power. Welcome to the hall.
It's empty. Let's build a working computer room, one piece at a time.
First piece: a {{rack|rack}}. It's a tall cabinet full of GPU chips. The chips do the computing that clients pay for.
Open Racks in the build bar. Pick the AC-1. Click the glowing spot.
after: There. Look at it. Dark. It has a cable under it, but nothing feeding the cable.

steps.text: Place the Grid Intake in the basement
say: A rack needs power. Power comes in through a Grid Intake. It's the plug into the city.
Open Power in the build bar. Pick Grid Intake. Click the glowing spot in the basement.
after: Lights on. The intake can give 1,500 kW.
A {{kw|kW}} is how hard something pulls right now. Your rack pulls up to 40 kW when it works.
The goal bar at the top shows it. LOAD is what the hall pulls. CAPACITY is what the intake can give.

steps.text: Place an air handler next to the rack
say: Cass. Cooling. Did you sleep? Never mind.
Every kW a rack uses turns into heat. A 40 kW rack is a 40 kW heater.
Too hot, and it slows down. Hotter still, and it shuts itself off.
An {{crah|air handler}} pulls the hot air away. Open Cooling. Pick the Air Handler. Click the glowing spot.
after: Good. The heat view is on. Red is hot, blue is cool.
Heat counts in kW too. Whatever the rack pulls, the air handler has to carry away.

steps.text: Watch the rack pick up its first job
say: A client just sent a job. A job is work for your racks to do.
Watch the rack pick it up.
after: Running. That's the whole loop. Power in, work done, heat out.
See PUE in the goal bar? {{pue|PUE}} is the hall's total power divided by what the racks use. 1.0 would be no waste.
Yours is higher. The air handler and the lift burn power too. Good halls keep PUE low.

steps.text: Keep it running cool for three hours
say: Let the clock run for three hours. Keep the rack busy and the temperature down.
I'll watch the meter. Cass will watch the heat.

lessons.learned: A {{rack|rack}} does the work. It needs power from the grid and cooling for its heat. Power is counted in {{kw|kW}}. {{pue|PUE}} shows how much extra the hall burns on top of the racks.
lessons.outro: That's a working hall. Power in, work done, heat out. Everything else is more of the same, bigger. Next, Luci will show you how it pays.
lessons.star2Text: At least 10% of the power was always spare while the rack ran.
lessons.star3Text: Not one minute without power once the first job started.

lessons.title: Earn Your Keep
lessons.concept: Earn: contracts pay for work. Jobs need running racks, storage for their data, and spare parts and bots to stay up.

steps.text: Accept the contract on the board
say: Luci Ferro. CFO. Call me Luci, Operator.
A rack that sits idle costs you. A rack that works pays you. That's the whole business.
Clients post contracts on the board. Open Contracts. Press C, or use the tab on the right.
This one is {{inference|inference}}. A client keeps asking a model questions, and pays every minute you keep up. Press Accept.
after: Once signed, your racks pick it up on their own. Money flows as soon as they run.

steps.text: Keep the racks running until the job pays
say: Now the only job is not breaking anything.
Power on, cooling on, racks working. Watch TREASURY at the top. Wait for the contract to end.
after: There. Paid. We need the revenue for our power and upkeep.
The PER HOUR figure at the top shows what's left.

steps.text: Place a Storage Array on the glowing spot
say: Cass. Did you see the new contract on the board? {{training|Training}}. One big job, paid when it's done.
It's worth more, and it brings a dataset: 1,000 TB. Try to accept it. Go on.
Refused? That's why: there's no room for the data. A job's data lives on a Storage Array.
Open Racks. Pick the Storage Array. It does no computing. It only holds data. Click the glowing spot.
after: Now there's room. Storage doesn't earn by itself. It lets the racks earn.

steps.text: Accept the training contract
say: Luci. Good. Now open Contracts and accept it.
A training job pays when it's finished, so be patient. If the storage ever goes dark, the job stalls. No data, no work.
after: Signed. The racks are on it.

steps.text: Buy spare parts in Supplies
say: Racks break. Something will break today. Something will tomorrow.
A broken rack earns nothing until it's fixed. A fix uses one spare part.
Open Supplies in the build bar. Buy 5 spare parts.
after: Good. They wait in the depot until they're needed.

steps.text: Buy a maintenance bot in Supplies
say: Parts sit in a depot. A bot carries one to the broken rack and fixes it.
Same tab. Buy a bot.
after: That's your repair crew. Parts in the depot. A bot to carry them.

steps.text: Let the training job finish
say: Last thing. Let the big job finish and take the money.

lessons.learned: {{inference|Inference}} pays while it runs. {{training|Training}} pays when it ends. Both need powered, cooled racks, and training also needs storage for its data. Spare parts and bots keep racks earning when something breaks.
lessons.outro: Two contracts paid. Racks busy, data stored, a crew on call. Next, Mel will show you how it grows.
lessons.star2Text: Both contracts were paid, and you finished with more cash than you started with.
lessons.star3Text: No job ever sat stalled for want of storage.

lessons.title: Grow the Tower
lessons.concept: Grow: research unlocks new ideas, Levels unlock bigger machines, and the Foreman builds for you.
lessons.goal: Research two ideas, reach Level 2, and switch on the Foreman.
lessons.passed: Level 2 reached and the Foreman at work

steps.text: Research Contract Automation
say: Hello. I'm Mel. Research. Sorry, I get nervous around new people.
Your racks earn research points, {{rp|RP}}. You spend them on new ideas. I've put 1,500 in the account to start.
Open Research. Press R, or use the tab on the right. Pick Contract Automation, then press Research.
after: Mm. Noted. That one is done. Ideas are permanent.

steps.text: Research Works Foreman
say: Ideas open other ideas. The next one is the Works Foreman. A builder who works for you.
It needs the first idea done, and it costs more. You have enough.
after: Two ideas done. Keep that in mind. You'll need exactly two for something else.

steps.text: Build two more racks
say: Luci. Levels. They're your company's rank. A higher Level opens bigger machines and pays a bonus.
Find the LEVEL bar at the top. Level 2 asks for two things. 120 PF of racks, and two ideas researched.
{{pflops|PF}} is how much computing a rack does. You have 80 PF. Two more racks make 120. Place two racks.
after: That's 120 PF. Both asks are met.

steps.text: Wait for Level 2
say: Levels are awarded at midnight. Let the clock run.
after: Level 2. For the record, that's a $3.75 million bonus. Spend it well.

steps.text: Switch on the Foreman in Automation
say: Now the Foreman. Open Automation. Press T, or use the tab on the right.
He builds for you. Racks when contracts need them. An air handler when racks run hot. Power when it runs short.
He spends your money, so he keeps a reserve you set. Switch him on but watch him.

lessons.learned: Research points buy new ideas. A Level needs enough PF of racks and enough ideas researched. The Foreman builds racks, cooling and power for you while you do something else.
lessons.outro: Hm. It's growing. That's what it wants. Where it goes is up to you.
lessons.star3Text: The Foreman is on, and cash never fell below his $1 million reserve.

lessons.title: The Three Trees
lessons.concept: The trees: racks are retrofitted down one of three trees. The Trees panel shows the next step.
lessons.goal: Retrofit a rack to Green, read the Trees panel, and earn your first Garden points.
lessons.passed: A Garden rack earned its first points

steps.text: Click a rack and retrofit it to Green
say: Bea again. Last lesson. This one's about how the whole ball of wax goes. That's the world, you idiot.
There are three ways, called trees. The Lattice: pure machines. The Flesh: living tissue. The Garden: clean power.
Each tree is a line of better racks. You join one by retrofitting. Click the rack that's glowing in the world. Its panel opens on the right.
Find Retrofit. Pick an upgrade path. The rack changes right where it stands.
after: There. An NM-1. It does 50 PF on 12 kW. The old one did 20 PF on 40 kW.
And now it counts. A plain rack scores for no tree. Only a retrofitted rack earns points.

steps.text: Open the Trees panel from the three bars at the top
say: Now the scoreboard. Click the three coloured bars at the top of the screen.
after: Three columns, one per tree. Each has its points, a ladder of racks, and a line that starts with Next.
That Next line is your to-do list. It names the research and the retrofit that come next.
The first tree to 1,000 points ends the game its way. Close the panel when you're done reading.

steps.text: Place PV Wall Panels in Power
say: Look at the Garden column again. It has a line about clean power.
Garden racks run at half speed on any power. Full speed only on clean power: sun and wind.
So give it some. Open Power. Pick PV Wall Panels. Click the glowing spot.
after: Panels in. The clean share climbs slowly. Check the Garden column later and watch the speed rise.

steps.text: Wait for the Garden's first points
say: Points come in once an hour, from racks that are busy.
Now let the clock run until the Garden scores.

lessons.learned: A plain rack scores for no tree. Retrofit it down a tree and it scores for that tree. The Trees panel lists each tree's next step. The Garden runs at half speed on any power and full speed on clean power.
lessons.outro: That's everything I got. Where you go is up to you. Nobody's stopping you. Go build your tower.
lessons.star2Text: A Green rack and clean power both standing when the first Garden points arrived.
lessons.star3Text: No minute without power, and no rack ran hotter than 80 degrees C.

lessons.title: Going Liquid
lessons.concept: Liquid cooling: a dense rack is cooled by water from a chiller and a CDU, not by air.
lessons.goal: Run a liquid-cooled rack for three hours without it overheating.
lessons.passed: A liquid-cooled rack ran cool for three hours
lessons.failed: A rack got too hot. The pipe, the chiller and the CDU all have to be in place and running. Have another go.

steps.text: Lay a coolant pipe along the glowing run
say: Cass. Cooling.
Air only goes so far. Past that, you need water. That's {{dlc|liquid cooling}}.
Water needs a pipe. Open Structure. Pick the Coolant pipe. Drag it along the glowing run.
after: Good. Now the water has somewhere to go.

steps.text: Place a Chiller on the glowing spot
say: A {{chiller|chiller}} makes the water cold.
Open Cooling. Pick the Chiller. Click the glowing spot.
after: It's big. It'll hum. You get used to it.

steps.text: Place a CDU on the glowing spot
say: Next, a {{cdu|CDU}}. It hands the cold water on to the racks.
Cooling again. Pick the Coolant Distribution Unit. Click the glowing spot.
after: The loop is done. Nothing is on it yet.

steps.text: Click the glowing rack and retrofit it to Synthetic
say: Now the rack. Click the one that's glowing. Its panel opens on the right.
Find Retrofit. Pick Synthetic. It becomes an LC-2, a liquid-cooled rack.
after: There. It sits on the pipe, so it can drink.

steps.text: Watch the Heat view while the rack takes a job
say: I've put the heat view on. Warm colours are hot racks.
A job is coming for it. Let's see if it stays cool.
after: It's working and it's cool. That's what water buys you.

steps.text: Keep it running for three hours
say: Three hours. Make sure it holds.

lessons.star2Text: The hall's PUE was 1.6 or lower at the end.
lessons.star3Text: No rack was throttled or tripped for heat.
lessons.learned: A liquid rack needs a loop: a coolant pipe, a {{chiller|chiller}} to cool the water and a {{cdu|CDU}} to hand it out. With the loop in place, a dense rack runs cool.
lessons.outro: That's liquid. Pipe, chiller, CDU, rack. Keep the water cold.

lessons.title: Lights Out
lessons.concept: Backup: a battery bank bridges the minutes after the grid drops, and a genset carries the racks for hours.
lessons.goal: Ride out a grid failure with no dark racks.
lessons.passed: The racks stayed lit through the outage
lessons.failed: The racks stayed dark too long. The battery and the genset have to be up and running before the grid drops. Have another go.

steps.text: Place a Battery Bank on the glowing spot
say: Bea. Power again. Today the grid goes out.
Not maybe. Today. So we get ready.
A {{ups|battery bank}} holds power for when the grid drops. Open Power. Pick the Battery Bank. Click the glowing spot.
after: Okay. Empty for now. It charges off the grid.

steps.text: Place a Diesel Genset on the glowing spot
say: Batteries don't last. Maybe an hour and a half at this load.
For longer you want an engine. A {{genset|genset}}. Diesel. Loud, and it burns money.
Open Power. Pick the Diesel Genset. Click the glowing spot.
after: Right. It starts itself when the grid runs short. It needs a few minutes to get up to speed.

steps.text: Check the Power view while the battery fills
say: I've put the power view on. That's where the load and the supply show.
Let the battery fill. Don't touch anything.
after: Full. Okay. Okay.
Hands off. Here it comes.

steps.text: Ride out the outage
say: There. Grid's gone.
The battery has the racks. The genset's waking up. Watch the load.
after: Genset's carrying them. The battery's topping up. Nobody went dark.
Grid's back. The genset stands down on its own.

steps.text: Keep the racks lit for half an hour
say: Give it half an hour. Make sure it holds.

lessons.star2Text: Not one minute without power during the outage.
lessons.learned: A {{ups|battery bank}} carries the racks for the minutes a {{genset|genset}} needs to start. The genset carries them for hours. Build both before the grid drops.
lessons.outro: That's how you keep the lights on. Build the backup before you need it.
